Create one full-bleed portrait 9:16 frame from a premium dimensional storybook South Indian wedding invitation film, solely from this written description. Intricately carved lifelike architecture with the refined illustrative finish of a cinematic animation, rich depth and atmospheric perspective. Honey-beige aged sandstone with dark brown carved recesses; ivory, deep red and antique gold accents. One warm sunrise from camera-left throughout, soft amber bloom with readable highlight detail, long diagonal shadows. Orange marigolds, white jasmine, green mango leaves, brass lamps, polished stone with warm directional reflections. No photographic humans, no watermark, no interface, no frame. Render only the exact text requested for this image. Materials and lighting stay consistent between an aerial view and a close view of the same site.

ONE temple complex with ONE dominant nine-tier sandstone gopuram with seven small finials at the far end of its central axis. In front of it is ONE much smaller freestanding square Ganesha mandap, with four carved square corner columns, a shallow stone roof with a low stepped pyramidal cap, a lotus relief on the front roof beam, three shallow front steps, and orange-white garland scallops. All four sides of the pavilion are OPEN BETWEEN THE COLUMNS, including the rear: clear daylight and the distant gopuram are visible through the rear gaps from a frontal low viewpoint. There is no masonry rear wall, inner sanctuary box, door panel, nested doorway, or second shrine inside. A single stationary Ganesha idol stands on the central low square lotus-carved pedestal. Two brass lamps stand to either side of the pedestal. Keep the roof, corner columns, steps, pedestal and rear opening physically consistent. The tower remains outside beyond the rear columns. The open left side connects directly to the adjacent invitation courtyard bay.

SHOT: EXTREME HIGH BIRD'S-EYE ESTABLISHING VIEW OF THE ENTIRE TEMPLE COMPLEX. The camera is far above the tallest gopuram, looking steeply DOWN at approximately 60 degrees below horizontal. This must read as a high drone looking onto rooftops, not a low drone looking horizontally at facades. Show the complete outer compound boundary with margins on all four sides, coconut groves surrounding it, both long side colonnades, the full gopuram, foreground water tank, and the small central Ganesha pavilion. Use the entire portrait composition for the temple and its surrounding landscape; no visible horizon is necessary. Warm sunrise comes from offscreen upper left, with long shadows, soft distant haze and an elegant grand sense of scale. The full compound fits within about 80 percent of frame width and 80 percent of frame height. The large tower is in the far upper-center of the compound; its entire roof and all finials are visible without cropping. The small central Ganesha pavilion is on the central axis below it, beyond the water tank, with its roof about 8-10 percent of frame width.

CRITICAL OCCUPIED PAVILION GEOMETRY: the small pavilion has the same four square carved corner columns, lotus front roof beam, low stepped stone roof cap, three shallow steps and orange-white garland scallops specified in the continuity description. It contains the SAME seated Ganesha on the central flower-covered pedestal, with two brass lamps. It is NOT an empty platform. From this steep overhead camera angle, the OPAQUE STONE ROOF PHYSICALLY BLOCKS THE LINE OF SIGHT to the statue's head and body. Show the roof's upper surface and the outer column edges below it; there is no clear frontal view through the pavilion from this high camera. A few garland ends and flower petals can be seen near the base, but no separately identifiable idol face. Do not draw an exposed empty opening or a bare unoccupied floor where the statue should be. The pavilion remains open on all four sides under its roof, with no rear wall or enclosed sanctuary box. The whole pavilion is small within the vast courtyard, ready for a camera to fly forward and descend under its roof. No additional central shrine, no new foreground pavilion, no giant floating idol, no text. Keep the path over the tank to this existing central pavilion unobstructed.
